_comment: Ground truth for the 55 synthetic postings in mock-postings-v3.json, used to measure the extraction pipeline (backend/extract.py) against a fixed target. Two things it is NOT. It is not a human label set -- see _not_a_label. And it is not one agent's opinion of each posting: every expected value carries the exact quoted substring of the posting that determines it, so a reader can audit the whole file against the corpus without trusting the author. That constraint exists because measuring a model against another model's unsupported assertion is the defect this effort was built to avoid (backend/tools/claude-bench.py:415-417 treats a single sonnet run as 'ground truth' and is the counter-example). Where a field is not determinable from what the model is shown, the value is null with a note saying what is absent; a null is an honest 'not measurable' and is worth more than a confident wrong answer.
_method: EVERY VALUE IS DERIVED FROM WHAT THE MODEL IS SHOWN, WHICH IS NOT THE WHOLE RECORD. build_prompt (extract.py:529-538) passes title, company, location, source and description only. The record's own `remote_policy` field is never shown, so it is used in this key as corroboration only, never as evidence, and never as a quote. || QUOTE RULE: every non-null quote is a byte-exact substring of the field named by quote_field, which defaults to description_text. Quotes are copied, never paraphrased, re-punctuated or normalised; a test verifies this mechanically and the file was validated against the corpus before it was written. A negative value (false, `none`) usually cannot be quoted -- you cannot quote an absence -- so those carry quote:null and a note naming what is missing. || FIELD DEFINITIONS COME FROM THE PROMPT (extract.py:322-372), NOT FROM INTUITION, so that a disagreement between key and model is an extraction error rather than a definitional argument. Four places where the prompt differs from the obvious reading, all followed as written: (1) years_experience_min is 'the smallest number of years the posting REQUIRES' (extract.py:339), so 'preferred', 'a plus' and 'up to one year' all record as null -- 41 of 55 rows are null for this reason and that is the correct answer, not missing data. (2) advanced_degree_required is true only for a REQUIRED Master's or PhD (extract.py:343), so a required bachelor's records as false -- see mock_042, where that is exactly what makes the verdict undecidable. (3) ml_research_required has three triggers -- publications, training from scratch, an advanced ML degree (extract.py:342) -- so fine-tuning an existing model does not qualify; mock_010 and mock_050 are false on that reading and both notes say so, because the field is priced -100 (a hard exclude) in config/pursuit-criteria.json and a false positive silently kills the row. (4) gap_friendly_language is true only for an EXPLICIT welcome of career breaks, returnships or non-traditional paths, 'not merely because it is entry-level' (extract.py:345). Only mock_002 and mock_045 qualify. NOTE THE CONFLICT: config/pursuit-criteria.json's _flags_comment reads the same flag more broadly for MATCHING ('no experience required', 'we will train'). The key follows the extraction prompt because that is what the model is asked for; the matcher's broader reading is a separate question and is not measured here. || remote_policy IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DOCTRINE CHOICE IN THIS FILE and an auditor should check it first. The word 'hybrid' appears in NO description in this corpus; 24 records carry remote_policy='hybrid' as metadata the model never sees. So the doctrine is: an explicit statement in the description wins ('This is an on-site role with weekend rotation', mock_016); failing that, a location of 'Remote ...' gives remote_local or remote_anywhere; failing that, duties that clearly imply physical presence (front desk, warehouse floor, production line, ticket window) give onsite, which extract.py:322 permits as 'clearly implies' and which was asserted only where the record's own metadata agreed; everything else is `unknown`. That yields 14 onsite, 4 remote_local, 4 remote_anywhere and 33 unknown. `unknown` is a real member of REMOTE_POLICY (extract.py:312-313), so this is the vocabulary's own answer for 'the posting does not say' rather than a dodge -- contrast seniority_level, where SENIORITY (extract.py:220-221) has NO unknown member and three gig postings therefore record null. A reader who thinks a city location plus office duties should read `onsite` will disagree with about thirty rows; that is why the doctrine is stated here rather than buried. || remote_local VS remote_anywhere IS UNDEFINED BY THE PROMPT. extract.py:335-347 gives field guidance for every enumerated field except ai_involvement and remote_policy, and docs/ingestion_tests/selfcheck-n120-2026-07-28.json shows 'remote_anywhere <-> remote_local' as the model's most frequent self-disagreement pair. This key reads a stated geographic bound ('candidates must be based in the US', 'Remote - United States') as remote_local and a bare 'Remote' with no bound as remote_anywhere, and says so in each note. || role_archetype: the support_ops / admin_ops boundary is NOT defined by the prompt, which distinguishes support_ops only from it_internal, by who is served (extract.py:337). This key uses the posting's own framing -- patient/guest/client services and public-facing intake are support_ops, records-and-processing work is admin_ops -- and names the runner-up in the notes on every row where the call was close. The distinction is nearly inert downstream: config/pursuit-criteria.json prices support_ops and implementation_analyst at 14 and admin_ops, marketing_ops and ai_operations at 12. `other` is what matters, at 0, and it was used only where no value in ARCHETYPE (extract.py:262-274) describes the role at all -- merchandise planning, insurance underwriting, revenue operations, logistics dispatch, business operations, data annotation. extract.py:337 is explicit that 'other' is a real answer. || location_is_nyc AND location_is_remote ARE NOT EXTRACTED FIELDS. lib/text.py:140-142 computes them from the location string at ingest. They are recorded here anyway because the cohort's location floor turns on them, and three rows disagree with the implementation ON PURPOSE: mock_022 and mock_030 (Long Island City) and mock_028 (Astoria) are in Queens, so the honest answer is true, but NYC_PATTERN (lib/text.py:25-28) matches only the borough names and 'new york' and will return false. Four further rows -- mock_017 Jersey City, mock_019 Yonkers, mock_029 Elizabeth NJ, mock_031 Newark NJ -- are commutable tri-state addresses that the pattern also misses; they are recorded good on their merits with the caveat in the entry notes, since config/pursuit-criteria.json charges location.neither_penalty (-15) rather than excluding them. || VERDICTS are against the cohort's shared floor -- entry-level, AI-adjacent, NYC or remote, no degree required (CLAUDE.md; config/pursuit-persona.json background_summary) -- not against any one Builder. 29 good, 25 bad, 1 undecided. The addendum's running total says 30 good and 25 bad; the difference is mock_042 alone, moved to undecided as instructed.
_field_provenance: TWO BLOCKS PER ENTRY, TWO DIFFERENT DENOMINATORS, AND THEY MUST NOT BE AVERAGED TOGETHER. `fields` holds the nine EXTRACTION targets -- the ones the model actually answers. `loader_fields` holds location_is_nyc and location_is_remote, which the model never sees a question about and never answers: the ingest loader computes them from the location string alone (lib/text.py:140-142). || THE PROOF IS IN ONE SELECT. match.py:275-281's _SELECT_FACTS pulls the nine as `f.` columns of job_facts and these two as `j.` columns of jobs, joined on j.id = f.job_id. Same row to a scorer, two different producers. || WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS TO THE HEADLINE NUMBER: scoring the model against the loader's flags would compare the loader's mapping of a ~20-character location string against this key's reading of the same string. They agree almost always, so folding them in would add 110 near-certain agreements to the numerator and inflate extraction accuracy with a field nobody extracted. That is a manufactured number and it is the same error in kind as the one _comment names. || THEY ARE KEPT, NOT DROPPED, because score_job reads them and config/pursuit-criteria.json prices them -- location.neither_penalty -15 and onsite_elsewhere_penalty -25. If the loader's mapping is wrong every row's score is wrong, and this key is the only artefact that would catch it. Measure them as a LOADER check with its own denominator (n=55 x 2), and expect three deliberate mismatches: mock_022 and mock_030 (Long Island City) and mock_028 (Astoria) are in Queens, which NYC_PATTERN (lib/text.py:25-28) does not match. Those three are the finding, not a defect in the key.
_not_a_label: This is a SPECIFICATION FIXTURE, not a human label. It must never be written into eval_labels and must never be merged with task 29's labels. See HANDOFF.md:805-808 -- fixtures written from a specification test the specification.
